speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: asked the Minister for Health in light of the new COVID-19 cases involving Singaporeans who have not been to China, what other measures can Singaporeans take to protect themselves from being infected by the coronavirus.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether there are any new insights on how COVID-19 is spread in light of the recent announcement of the cluster of local transmission; and (b) whether there are heightened concerns now of a community spread of the virus in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think it will be useful for me to give a quick update of the situation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Coronavirus Disease of 2019 (COVID-19) situation continues to evolve globally and locally.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Of the 53 cases still in hospital, most are stable or improving.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Four are in critical condition in the intensive care unit.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Contact tracing has helped us to identify five clusters and investigations on these clusters are ongoing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Contact tracing is underway for the other seven locally transmitted cases to establish any links to previous cases or travel history to mainland China.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Since early January, we have progressively put in place precautionary measures to detect and limit the transmission of the virus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These include travel controls, contact tracing and placing identified close contacts under quarantine.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The PHPCs will provide subsidised care for patients with respiratory illnesses in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We observed that several of the locally confirmed cases had remained in the community or gone to work even when they were ill.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We urge individuals with respiratory symptoms, such as fever, cough, sore throat and runny nose, to seek medical treatment at PHPCs or polyclinics early and stay home throughout their MC period.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I am also heartened to see many ground-up initiatives to support our frontline healthcare workers, the needy and vulnerable groups, as well as the affected patients and their families.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This whole-of-society spirit is essential in building a resilient nation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When we stand united, we will prevail, and I am glad to see Members wearing this SG United button.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Let us stay united as we battle this disease.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Knowledge of COVID-19 is still evolving as scientists around the world work to better understand the virus.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: MOH studies the latest reports, consults international infectious diseases experts and keeps in touch with other health authorities to gain greater knowledge of the virus and how it is transmitted.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The current medical assessment still points to COVID-19 spreading mainly through droplets and physical contact from an infected person.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Based on evidence available in China, an expert from the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention has said that there is currently no evidence that the virus can be transmitted through aerosol.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Individually, we can each play a part to curb the spread of disease through socially responsible practices.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Observing good personal hygiene, such as washing our hands with soap and water regularly, and not touching our face and eyes, remains the key means by which individuals can protect themselves and reduce the risk of transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Each person should also monitor his or her health closely, take temperature twice daily, see a doctor when unwell and stay home to rest, and if they must go out, for example, to see a doctor, wear a mask.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We expect to see more cases in Singapore, partly as a result of enhanced surveillance we put in place recently.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We must be prepared for the possibility of wider community spread.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will continue to monitor the situation and prepare for different scenarios I sketched out during the Ministerial Statement at the last Sitting.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will also finetune and adjust our measures accordingly as the situation evolves.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Together, with everyone playing our part and staying united, we are confident that we will overcome this outbreak and emerge stronger as a nation.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But of late, some of the activities seem to suggest that people are reacting in a slightly different manner.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When the Development Bank of Singapore (DBS) had a case, they evacuated people from the whole of the floor at Marina Bay Financial Centre (MBFC).

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am just wondering what is the advice from MOH to the rest of the people?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Do we carry on with our lives or should we react whenever a case comes up?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Should buildings evacuate the buildings' occupants when they find that there is someone who had been in contact with an infected person?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, we have been briefing those who have been affected, including corporations, entities, organisations.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I had mentioned, last week, I met the religious leaders, church leaders to explain to them what are the precautions they can put in place.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As the Prime Minister said, life must go on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have to continue as normally as possible while taking the necessary precautions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are the types of advice we have given to the churches.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Depending on the situation, different organisations may adopt different measures where practical and, if they are in doubt, we have also invited them to contact us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have done the same to the other religious organisations – the Buddhist organisation, the Taoist organisation, the Hindu organisation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are reaching out to them and any organisations that have questions or are uncertain as to what they should do, they can contact us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When a case is identified as positive, we will also inform the organisation to do the necessary cleaning and disinfection and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Sometimes, organisations may overreact and take upon themselves to do things that may not be necessary and may cause misunderstandings.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we advise organisations that when there is a confirmed case, if they are not sure, to consult us or to consult the National Environment Agency (NEA) which oversees the environmental cleaning processes.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This way, we will then be able to react calmly and respond effectively to any confirmed cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I would advise organisations that are uncertain to please contact us.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We will provide the necessary guidance and advice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I just have one specific question on the effectiveness of temperature screening because this has caused a lot of surge in the demand for thermometers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: More importantly, whether it is actually effective because some of the patients that have been discovered, showed very mild symptoms.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am really not sure if it is the best way.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The other thing is, there have also been reports about how there were some faulty infrared thermometers that were not very accurate.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, I just want the Minister's thoughts on this and the guidelines that can be given to the organisations on this matter.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Individually, it is also important for you to take temperature regularly so that you know whether you are well or unwell.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But very often, you also find that individuals know that they are unwell even if they do not have a temperature.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is also evidenced from the studies that show that, for COVID-19, sometimes, the high temperature comes much later, in the later part of your illness.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Or come to our polyclinics for a proper assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Once we have made the assessment, if we find that you are at risk, we will then refer you to the hospitals for assessment and testing.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If your symptoms recover within those five days, well and good.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If not, please go back to the same doctor.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you go to a different doctor, they may not know the history and you have to repeat all over again, and you may have missed out certain indications.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We encourage you to go back to the same doctor so that there is a continuity of care.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This way, we will help to minimise transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But if you do not have a temperature, it does not mean that you are perfectly well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We still have to make an assessment, whether you feel well or unwell.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For organisations, we also advise them, even after they have taken the temperature, observe the individual.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If he does not look well, please advise him to go back and rest, rather than rely solely on temperature-taking.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I just have two clarifications about the Disease Outbreak Response System Condition (DORSCON) level – the acronym of the year, so far!

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, some clarification about how this DORSCON is arrived at.

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Is it by independent committee that makes this decision and recommends to the Minister?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The second question which I think many Singaporeans would be interested in is what are the parameters by which the DORSCON level may be adjusted?

speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In this case, specifically, what are the parameters under which they would consider lowering it from Orange to Yellow?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The conditions for DORSCON levels are published on our website.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: At the end of the day, we would need to make a judgement.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In making the judgement, we have to take into account inputs from the professionals, inputs from the community and make an assessment of the situation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, there are multiple factors that need to be considered.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is not just counting the numbers and ticking the boxes before we decide to switch either way.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Taskforce will assess and recommend, and eventually, the Minister for Health is the one who declares the DORSCON level.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Whenever I hold a press conference, rumours will fly around that we are going to go to DORSCON Red.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Every time, we would have to spend resources and efforts to address the rumours.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, please help us not to spread rumours that are untrue.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Again, as we continue to monitor the situation, there may be a time when we will have to adjust the DORSCON level downwards to Yellow or to Green.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Again, we will take into account multiple factors – the number of infections that we are seeing, the severity of the diseases and whether or not the viral transmission is able to be controlled.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, there are many factors that we will consider, including outside Singapore, what is the situation globally.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is eventually a judgement, taking into account all the various relevant factors.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Pritam Singh who is sitting next to the Member in red.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My first question is how many individuals does the Government expect to be transitioning into this Stay-Home Notice regime?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because a lot of these individuals, as Members know, would be living in the community, in households, in Housing and Development Board flats and so forth.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second question is, there would ostensibly be a higher chance of community spread, in view of these returnees.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We call them, we have video calls as well and we also track their location, where they are.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will help us to reduce the manpower resources that we need to ensure that they stay at home.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is a step-up from the Leave of Absence (LOA) that we have introduced, where they were allowed to go out occasionally for meals and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think this is the enforcement regime, which was explained yesterday.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Speaker, I have to first commend MOH for putting up a lot of timely information and good information for people's use.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: But, as the Minister rightly pointed out, rumours and also misinformation can create unnecessary fear and panic.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: There are, of course, a lot of closed chat groups now.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I just wonder if the Minister can shed some light as to whether any actions will be taken against those who intentionally spread some of the information that creates the panic that goes around.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I was actually asked to evacuate my building the other day because the office building apparently had an ambulance that came by.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We encourage Members or members of the public, if you come across any of these closed chat groups, if the information does not look real, please check with us, go to gov.sg, wait for the notices to be sent to you through WhatsApp, those are accurate, official information.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And we have been sharing as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: All that we know, we share with the public.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We have daily press briefings and occasional press conferences by Ministers and regular updates from time to time, even within the day.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, rest assured that we will provide as much information as possible, once we obtain it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There is no need to second guess what the situation is.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you do come across messages or statements that look suspicious, that cannot be verified, please do not forward them to your friends.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You may find that amusing or entertaining, but please refrain from forwarding because this will then multiply.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you find that they are suspicious and you are not sure, do forward it to us and we will check on whether they are correct or not and we will let you know the details.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we have to deal with it one by one, there is no easy solution.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But each of us can play our part by not forwarding unverified information, and informing the authorities if you come across any of them.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Speaker, I would like to ask the Minister, there are quite a lot of cases where the person that has it goes to the general practitioner (GP) or polyclinic a few times and only on the third or fourth visit, was he then referred to the acute hospital for the test.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Does it make sense to make the test kits available at least at the polyclinics or some of the GPs so that they can test earlier?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Because in one case, the person, from the onset of symptoms until he went to the National University Hospital (NUH), it was almost 10 days.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, throughout that period, he could be spreading to a lot of people.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is not possible to test all 30,000 of them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On top of that, you may have a lot of false positives that you have to chase around.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, the best way for us is for the doctors to make a clinical judgement as they see the patients.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they find that you have signs of pneumonia, then they will refer the patient to the hospital for assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If it is the normal common cough and cold, you are likely to have recovered within these four or five days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will reduce the amount of noise in the system to allow us to identify cases that are more likely to be problematic.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even for those who do not recover within these five days, it does not mean that you have COVID-19 because there are still a lot of other possible infections that you may be suffering from.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In fact, a very small number everyday will be COVID-19-positive.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, therefore, if you are asked to stay home with a five-day MC, do not panic, it does not mean you definitely have COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is a means for you to stay at home to rest, to minimise transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will also help by reducing the normal cough and cold transmission, if you stay at home and recover, rather than move around in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I also encourage individuals, when you are sick, if you have not recovered within these five days, please go back to the same doctor, rather than to move from doctor to doctor and then we have less ability to track the history.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is the advice I would give to individuals: if you are ill and not well, see a doctor.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If the doctor gives you an MC, stay at home throughout the MC period, do not go around and do not go and queue up to buy toilet paper and so on.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Please stay home and, if you need help, there is always the MOH hotline that you can call if you need some help.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If you are very ill and you need the ambulance, you can always call for the ambulance and we will convey you to the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When you finish your MC, if you are still unwell, go back to see the same doctor and the doctor will then be in a position to make a clinical judgement whether or not you should be sent to the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our doctors are well-trained and they are familiar with the assessments they need to do on the ground.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is also not appropriate to ask our primary care doctors to do the test because it requires swabs and special techniques.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of the doctors may not be familiar with how to do that and it also exposes the doctors unnecessarily to potential infection because swabbing can be quite a hazardous process.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is better done in a hospital environment so that our trained professionals will be able to do it properly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some private hospitals are planning to do that because they are also trained and they also have the equipment and the facilities to do so safely.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are working with the private hospitals to also allow the private hospitals to do some of these testing in order for us to share the patient load.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Speaker, I would like to ask the Minister for Health pertaining to the guideline on the five-day MC.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: We understand the reasoning behind the five-day recommendation and also how we will assess in giving this MC.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: However, there has been many misinterpretation perhaps and spinoffs from these five days and I am asking this question on behalf of frontline healthcare workers.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Because people are now coming and demanding, "Why is it just three days and not five days?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: MOH says it is compulsory for you to give us five days".

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: So, therefore, we make the decision based on clinical judgement and case-by-case basis.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: We understand the five days and we understand that if you do have upper respiratory tract symptoms with fever and all that, and even with no travel history, the five days are definitely justifiable.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But for others who may not have all the components of the symptoms, but there are other problems, I hope that the Minister can reinforce that it is really up to us on a case-by-case basis to decide on this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For example, the patient might have already been ill for four days, and so, there is no need to give another five days.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is the clinical judgement of the doctor.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We said five days and this is a guideline given to the doctors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We encourage doctors to exercise their judgement and we also want Singaporeans to know and to trust the doctors' judgement.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our doctors are well-trained and they know what to do.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Please do not ask him to come back to work, because by coming back to work, if he has the virus, it may actually be exposed to your other employees and your whole company may be affected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is in the interest of the employees to rest at home so that they can recover quickly and it is also in the interest of the employers to ensure that their employees, the workers, stay at home and rest rather than come to work.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I also want to take this opportunity to seek the support of our employers to allow us to implement these guidelines so as to minimise the transmission in the community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Speaker, I have noticed during my walkabouts in my constituency, in some GP clinics, the receptionists wear masks and the nurses wear masks.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But in some GP clinics, it could be just next to the one where the nurses wear masks, they do not don masks at all.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, are there some guidelines for the GP clinics to follow?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think that the clinic managers and the GPs know exactly what to do.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For those who are patient-facing and potentially have a risk of exposure to potential COVID-19 or other infectious diseases, they would usually wear masks.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And sometimes, if their clinics are more for health screening and so on, they are less likely to encounter patients with these illnesses or infectious diseases, they may not need to wear a mask.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we leave it to the clinics to make a judgement, but we would encourage them that where they have a risk of facing patients who potentially have infectious diseases, including COVID-19, they ought to wear a mask to protect themselves as well as to protect the patients because they may inadvertently pass on the disease to the patient as well.

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: In the recent press conference, Minister Lawrence Wong said that COVID-19 is less deadly, more infectious and it is more like Hemagglutinin 1 and Neuraminidase 1 (H1N1) than severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS).

speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
text: I have got some feedback asking if this means we have to prepare for the long haul, and how long is "long"; and whether we will get back to normal day-to-day life.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Maybe I should ask Minister Lawrence Wong to answer this question, but let me try to answer the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think what Minister Lawrence Wong intended to say is that, in terms of statistics, based on today's evidence, that transmissibility seems to be much faster, much higher, quite close to H1N1.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And therefore, we do expect a significant number of cases both globally as well as in Singapore in time to come.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And therefore, it is quite different in terms of fatality compared to SARS.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is the nature of the disease, and the knowledge of the disease is still evolving, as I mentioned in my reply, and the scientists are still discovering new things about the disease.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And H1N1 is still with us today; occasionally, we still see cases of H1N1.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We may have to learn to live with it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is why, even today, we are encouraging Singaporeans to live life as normal as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Life must go on, take the necessary precautions, but we can continue to live normally as much as possible so that there is no need to have drastic shifts from one way to the other.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But precautions like temperature taking, seeing a doctor when unwell, these are normal precautions which, in fact, even without COVID-19 or H1N1, we should be practising.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This is also an opportunity for us to reinforce these socially responsible practices, ensure that when we are sick, see a doctor and observe personal hygiene practices, wash your hands frequently.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It does not mean that once COVID-19 is over, if it is ever over, we stop washing hands.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: The Senior Activity Centres (SACs) which actually serve many of the elderly, especially in rental estates, are instructed to wind down many of their activities in order to protect the elderly.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Some of us on the ground find that many of these elderly residents are loitering around and they are no more exercising.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I wonder if the Minister's message to live life as normally as possible could be extended to the beneficiaries of SACs.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Indeed, Mr Speaker, we do want SACs to continue as much as possible.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is also important that some SACs and organisations have temporarily suspended some of the activities in order for them to put in place some precautionary measures.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Some of the measures may need time for them to set up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In times like this, exercise is important to keep ourselves healthy and resilient.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, we do want to encourage the activities and exercises to continue with the necessary precautions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, rather than being in the coffee shops, we might as well organise them in the SACs so that we are able to manage them to prevent transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We take the Member's point fully and will work with the various organisations to do that.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Supposing a worker who has just come back from China has been issued with a Stay-Home Notice and he breaches his Stay-Home Notice in that he deliberately ignores the notice and he goes out, what is the risk to the community that he may carry the COVID-19 virus and spread it to the community at large?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: What is MOH's assessment of the risk to the people who may meet up with him in the community?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, let me explain that there are different categories of people who are served certain notices and orders.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For those who are ill with COVID-19, confirmed cases, all of them are in the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, once they are confirmed, they are treated in the isolation wards in the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are not running around in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But at the same time, once we have identified a positive case, we identify the contacts of these positive cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are the people who have been with the confirmed cases for an extended period of time and they are potentially exposed.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These people are served with what we call quarantine orders.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For quarantine orders, there are strict rules for compliance and there are staff and officers who will do surveillance and make sure that they are in our quarantine centres.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are also very strict orders under the Infectious Diseases Act and they have the full force of the law to ensure that they stay under the home quarantine orders.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But I also need to emphasise that these people who are served quarantine orders are not sick.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are exposed to persons who are sick but they themselves are not down with COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Once they have symptoms, because they are under close surveillance, they will be immediately conveyed to the hospital for treatment and follow-up.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, again, if they become one of the confirmed cases, they will be treated in the hospital.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There will be a group of people like those returning from China.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They were exposed in the community but they do not have direct contact with a potential case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, their risk level is significantly lower than the close contacts of confirmed cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, they are served these Stay-Home Notices to allow them to stay at home, minimise contact with the outside community to minimise the risk of spread.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: These are generally healthy people and they do not have immediate known contacts with confirmed cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, as a precaution, we want them to stay at home.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, it suggests that a mild case seen by a GP and told to stay at home and rest, that case will progress, the person will recover but it will never be detected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, I wonder whether this could actually be a good thing because, internationally, we have been called the "gold standard" in detection.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: But, now, it is perhaps giving us an undue reputation for risks when actually we may not have that many real cases compared to many other countries.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I think the conclusion is the other way around.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But other countries may have more cases than what they have reported.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member is right that some of the cases may have mild symptoms.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But, generally, they may last quite some time and, therefore, after five days, if you have not yet recovered, then we are suspicious of you.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even then the doctors have to make a clinical judgement.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It does not necessarily mean that once you have pneumonia, you will be referred and, if you do not have pneumonia, they will rule it out.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The doctor will make a clinical judgement based on your condition and history, whether you have been in contact with multiple groups of people that have been exposed, for example.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They also want to take your history, whether you have indirect contacts.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The doctors are well-trained and very experienced in making clinical assessments.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I have said, we cannot test 30,000 cases every day.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This will allow us to have a sense of what is happening on the ground in reality and give us a sense of judgement of how the situation is evolving.
